_comment: Cross-layer vocabularies with a single owner. A concept that appears in a Python domain enum, a TypeScript wire contract and an API payload has three lifecycles and no owner, and forks silently -- each fork is locally reasonable and nothing detects that the same concept now has two definitions. These are generated into shared/governance/vocabularies.py and checked against packages/schemas/canonical/index.ts, and check_vocabularies.py refuses a second definition elsewhere in the tree.

vocabularies.name: EvidenceLevel
vocabularies.docstring:
Causal evidence ladder.

ADR-0004 D3: absence is not a tier. A value of ``None`` means the evidence was
never assessed, and it must stay distinguishable from ``L0``, which is a
measurement -- anecdotal, but taken. No member of this enum may be used as a
default for an unassessed claim.

Assessability is orthogonal and travels alongside as a separate boolean; see
modules/adlift/domain/incrementality.py, where ``assessable`` is a field of its
own rather than a level.

members.name: L0_ANECDOTAL
members.comment: anecdotal: treatment observed, nothing to compare against

members.name: L2_MATCHED_DESCRIPTIVE
members.comment: matched control but pre-trend/balance not clean

vocabularies.name: JobStatus
vocabularies.docstring:
Terminal and in-flight states of a long-running job.

PARTIAL is the state a job reaches when some of its work succeeded and some did
not. Without it such a job has to be recorded as either succeeded or failed,
and both are wrong in a way the caller cannot see.

members.name: PARTIAL
members.comment: some work completed and some did not; neither succeeded nor failed

known_forks.definition: QUEUED / RUNNING / RETRYING / SUCCEEDED / FAILED / CANCELLED / DEAD_LETTER (uppercase)
known_forks.note: A second job-status vocabulary: different casing, two extra states, and also missing PARTIAL. RETRYING and DEAD_LETTER are queue mechanics rather than job outcomes, which is arguably a separate concept that should be named as one.
The closest to canonical, missing only PARTIAL. Migrating it to the generated enum is the smaller of the two moves.
